'''Julia Chuzhoy''' ({{Langx|he|ג'וליה צ'וז'וי}}) is an Israeli mathematician and computer scientist at the [[Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago]],{{r|cv}} known for her research on [[approximation algorithm]]s and [[graph theory]].

==Education and career==
Chuzhoy earned bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees from the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] in 1998, 2000, and 2004 respectively.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, on approximation algorithms, was supervised by [[Joseph Seffi Naor|Seffi Naor]].{{r|mg}} She has been at the Toyota Technological Institute since 2007,{{r|cv}} and also holds a position in the Computer Science Department of the [[University of Chicago]].{{r|icm2}}

==Contributions and recognition==
Chuzhoy won the best paper award at the 2012 [[Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science]] for her paper with Shi Li on approximating the problem of connecting many given pairs of vertices in a graph by edge-disjoint paths.{{ran|CL12}}{{r|ttic}}{{r|focs}}
She is also known for her work showing a polynomial relation between the size of a [[grid graph]] [[graph minor|minor]] of a graph and its [[treewidth]].{{ran|CC16}}{{r|godel}} This connection between these two graph properties is a key component of the [[Robertson–Seymour theorem]], is closely related to [[Halin's grid theorem]] for infinite graphs, and underlies the theory of [[bidimensionality]] for graph approximation algorithms.

She was an Invited Speaker at the 2014 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in [[Seoul]].{{r|icm|icm2}}
